questions.question_text: Choose the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'Ephemeral'.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time; Eternal means lasting or existing forever, making it the antonym.

options: Neither the manager nor the employees was aware of the change.
Neither the manager nor the employees were aware of the change.
Neither the manager nor the employees is aware of the change.
Neither the manager nor the employees has been aware of the change.
questions.explanation: According to the rule of proximity, when using 'neither/nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. Since 'employees' is plural, the verb must be 'were'.
Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; scrupulous shares this meaning of being very careful and precise.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence with the correct use of a semicolon.
options: I have a big test tomorrow; therefore, I cannot go out tonight.
I have a big test tomorrow; and I cannot go out tonight.
I have a big test tomorrow; I will stay home; studying.
I have a big test tomorrow, therefore; I cannot go out tonight.
questions.explanation: A semicolon is used to connect two independent clauses linked by a conjunctive adverb like 'therefore'.

questions.question_text: Which word is the correct spelling?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling requires double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct idiom to complete the sentence: 'After failing the exam, he realized he had to __________'.
questions.explanation: Going 'back to the drawing board' means starting over because a previous attempt failed.

questions.question_text: Which of these words is a noun?
questions.explanation: Grace is a noun (a quality), while graceful is an adjective and graciously is an adverb.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct preposition: 'She has been working here __________ 2015.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used to denote a starting point in time.

questions.question_text: Which phrase is the most formal way to say 'I'll look into it'?
options: I will get back to you.
questions.explanation: In professional academic or business contexts, 'investigate the matter' is more formal than colloquial phrases.

questions.question_text: Identify the word that acts as a conjunction.
questions.explanation: 'Although' is a subordinating conjunction used to introduce a dependent clause.
Eloquent means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing; articulate is a synonym.

questions.question_text: Correct the sentence: 'Each of the students were happy with their grade.'
options: Each of the students was happy with their grade.
Each of the students were happy with his grade.
Each of the students were happy with its grade.
Each of the students was happy with his or her grade.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so it requires a singular verb 'was' and gender-neutral singular pronouns.

questions.question_text: Identify the sentence that correctly uses a participial phrase.
options: Walking down the street, the trees were beautiful.
Walking down the street, I noticed the beautiful trees.
The trees were beautiful, walking down the street.
While walking down the street, the trees appeared beautiful.
questions.explanation: A participial phrase must modify the subject of the main clause. In this case, 'I' is the one walking, not the trees.

questions.question_text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The CEO's decision was __________, leaving no room for further debate.'
questions.explanation: Peremptory means final, absolute, and not open to challenge or delay.
